issues.legal_issue: A municipal property assessment cannot determine annual rental value by applying a flat rate per unit of floor area without a basis for treating the properties as comparable and deriving a reasonable annual rent.
material_facts: The municipality assessed textile mills and other special properties using fixed rental rates per 100 square feet of floor area.

The properties differed in location, age, construction and other characteristics, and the municipality did not establish that the factories were sufficiently similar for a floor-area method to provide a sound rental valuation.
The municipality did not show that it had derived the rate from the contractor's method or another recognised valuation method.
The governing scheme required the rateable value of each property to be based on the annual rent for which it might reasonably be expected to let from year to year.
issues.conclusion: The flat floor-area method was contrary to the Act and the taxation rules; the relevant assessments were invalid and fresh assessment lists had to be prepared.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(53), 2(54) and 127(3) of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, read with rule 7(1) and rule 9(b), required rateable value to be determined by reference to reasonable annual rent. In Lokmanya Mills v. Barsi Borough Municipality, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 306, the Court held that a municipality could not substitute an arbitrary floor-area valuation for a valuation based on a recognised method tied to annual rental value. The floor-area method may be appropriate where properties are sufficiently alike, but it cannot be applied indiscriminately.

rule.if: property_tax_assessment_proceeding and rental_value_required and flat_floor_area_rate_used and properties_not_shown_to_be_comparable

predicates.property_tax_assessment_proceeding: The proceeding challenges a municipal assessment of property tax.
predicates.rental_value_required: The applicable assessment scheme requires rateable value to be based on the reasonable annual rent of the property.
predicates.flat_floor_area_rate_used: The assessing authority determined rental value by applying a fixed rate to each unit of floor area.
predicates.properties_not_shown_to_be_comparable: The assessing authority did not establish that the properties were sufficiently alike for the same floor-area rate to provide a reliable rental valuation.

issues.definition: When a property-tax assessment proceeding concerns a scheme requiring reasonable annual rent, a flat floor-area rate applied without showing that the properties are comparable makes the assessment invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Applying a uniform floor-area valuation to dissimilar properties without rational classification violates the constitutional guarantee of equality.
material_facts: The municipality applied floor-area rates to factories that differed in location, age and construction.
There was no rational classification of the factories that could justify applying the same rates to properties with materially different rental characteristics.
The municipality divided buildings into processing and non-processing categories without establishing a rational basis for that distinction.
issues.conclusion: The assessment method, as applied, violated Article 14 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 prohibits unequal treatment resulting from an arbitrary or irrational classification. Lokmanya Mills v. Barsi Borough Municipality, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 306, was relied on concerning the arbitrary use of floor area to value dissimilar properties. Bhuvaneswariah v. State, A.I.R. 1965 Mys. 170, and N. Kunhali Haji v. State of Kerala, A.I.R. 1966 Ker. 14, were referred to in relation to the inequality that can result from taxation based on floor area without rational classification.

predicates.property_tax_assessment_proceeding: The proceeding challenges a municipal assessment of property tax.
predicates.dissimilar_properties_given_uniform_floo: The assessing authority applied the same floor-area rates to properties that differed in characteristics relevant to their rental value.
predicates.no_rational_classification: The assessing authority did not classify the properties on a rational basis that justified the different or uniform treatment.

issues.definition: An assessment violates equal protection when, in a property-tax assessment proceeding, dissimilar properties receive uniform floor-area treatment without a rational classification.

issues.legal_issue: A tax on machinery cannot be imposed as a tax on land or buildings when the legislature's taxing authority extends only to land and buildings.
material_facts: The taxation rules treated specified plant and machinery situated in or on land or buildings as part of the property for fixing rateable value.
The resulting property tax included machinery, even though the machinery was located in or on the building for use in operating the factory.
The relevant legislative taxing authority extended to taxes on land and buildings.
issues.conclusion: Rule 7(2), insofar as it authorised taxation of plant and machinery as part of land or buildings, was beyond the legislative competence of the State.
issues.legal_principle: Entry 49 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution authorises taxes on land and buildings, not on machinery merely because it is situated in or on a building. In re The Central Provinces and Berar Act No. XIV of 1938, [1939] F.C.R. 18, and Diamond Sugar Mills Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh, [1961] 3 S.C.R. 242, were considered on the limits of construing legislative entries: they are read broadly, but not beyond the reasonable meaning of their words. Ralla Ram v. Province of East Punjab, [1948] F.C.R. 207, was also considered in relation to legislative competence and taxation.

predicates.property_tax_assessment_proceeding: The proceeding challenges a municipal property-tax assessment.
predicates.machinery_included_in_property_tax: The assessment treats machinery situated in or on a property as part of the taxable property.
predicates.taxing_power_limited_to_land_and_buildin: The relevant taxing authority extends to land and buildings but not to machinery merely because it is situated there.

issues.definition: A property tax exceeds legislative competence when it includes machinery in a tax whose authority is limited to land and buildings.

issues.legal_issue: A rule that gives an official unguided discretion to specify taxable classes of machinery, without an effective appeal, is invalid for excessive delegation.
material_facts: The rules empowered the Commissioner, with the Corporation's approval, to specify classes of machinery to be treated as part of land or buildings for valuation.
The rules provided no principle to guide which machinery classes could be specified.
The Commissioner was the only decision-maker on the specification, and no right of appeal against the specification was provided.
issues.conclusion: Rule 7(3) was invalid because the legislature had excessively delegated power.
issues.legal_principle: The legislature may not delegate a power without providing guiding principles for its exercise. The Court held that the power to specify machinery classes depended on the Commissioner's arbitrary choice and that the absence of a right of appeal reinforced the defect. The judgment does not rely on an earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: property_tax_assessment_proceeding and official_can_select_taxable_machinery_classes and no_guiding_standard and no_appeal_from_selection

predicates.property_tax_assessment_proceeding: The proceeding challenges rules used to determine the property subject to municipal taxation.
predicates.official_can_select_taxable_machinery_cl: An official has power to decide which classes of machinery are treated as taxable property.
predicates.no_guiding_standard: The rule supplies no principle or standard to guide the official's selection of machinery classes.
predicates.no_appeal_from_selection: The affected person has no right of appeal against the official's selection.

issues.definition: A machinery-classification rule is invalid when, in a property-tax assessment proceeding, an official may select taxable machinery classes without a guiding standard or an appeal from that selection.

issues.legal_issue: A prior judgment does not bar consideration of a constitutional challenge that the earlier court rejected for inadequate pleading without deciding on its merits.
material_facts: Some mills had previously challenged assessments in proceedings before a High Court.
That court rejected the discrimination and equality submissions because they had not been specifically pleaded and therefore did not decide those submissions on their merits.
The later proceedings raised the equality challenge with the relevant specific allegations.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment did not operate as res judicata against the equality challenge.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated an issue as not barred by res judicata where the earlier court rejected it for insufficient pleading and did not adjudicate it on its merits. No earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.later_property_tax_challenge: A proceeding raises a challenge to a municipal property-tax assessment after an earlier proceeding concerning the assessment.
predicates.earlier_judgment_rejected_issue_for_inad: The earlier court rejected the relevant issue because it had not been sufficiently pleaded.
predicates.earlier_judgment_did_not_decide_issue_on: The earlier court did not determine the substance of the relevant issue.

issues.definition: An earlier judgment does not bar an issue in a later property-tax challenge when the earlier court rejected it for inadequate pleading without deciding its substance.
